title: How does a lighthouse throw light so far?
question: A lighthouse flame shines in every direction and a solid lens big enough to focus it would be impossibly thick. How did lighthouses reach the horizon?
answer: Augustin Fresnel cut away the thick middle of the lens and kept only the light-bending curves as rings of glass prisms around the lamp, gathering scattered light into one beam visible more than 20 miles out; the same stepped rings are in car tail lights today.
problem: Lighthouse lamps lost half their light or more, and a solid lens to fix it would be enormous and swallow light.
solution: Fresnel's stepped lens: only the curved surfaces, as rings of prisms, focusing the flame into one far-reaching beam.
surprise: The same stepped rings are in the car tail light in front of you.

c1.text: Before the Fresnel lens, lamps with reflectors lost much of their light: reflectors returned only about half the light (Wikipedia), a reflector light lost 60-80 % (NPS); an open flame scatters light in all directions.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Hatteras, 'The Fresnel Lens', https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/fresnellens.htm

c2.text: A conventional solid glass lens big enough for a lighthouse would be enormous, heavy and impractical; early thick lenses lost light in the glass.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Fresnel lens' (Rogers lenses 14 cm thick, absorption), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresnel_lens

c3.text: Fresnel's lens removes the thick interior and keeps the light-bending surfaces as concentric stepped rings / prisms, gathering scattered light into one beam.
sources: National Park Service, Cape Hatteras, 'The Fresnel Lens', https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/fresnellens.htm

c4.text: The first lighthouse Fresnel lens was lit at Cordouan, France, in July 1823 (25 July 1823).
sources: Phare de Cordouan (French Ministry of Culture), 'Cordouan's first lens', https://cordouan.culture.gouv.fr/en/cordouans-first-lens

c5.text: A Fresnel lighthouse light could shine to the horizon, more than 20 miles out (Cordouan 1823: >32 km / 20 mi; large first-order lenses ~21 miles).
sources: National Park Service, Cape Hatteras, 'The Fresnel Lens', https://www.nps.gov/caha/learn/historyculture/fresnellens.htm
Wikipedia, 'Fresnel lens' (Cordouan visible more than 32 km), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresnel_lens

c6.text: Fresnel lenses are used today in car lights (tail, marker, reversing lights; plastic Fresnel lenses in lamps) and some traffic signals.
sources: Wikipedia, 'Fresnel lens' (tail, marker and reversing lights), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresnel_lens
Explain that Stuff, 'Fresnel lenses' (car lamps, traffic signals), http://www.explainthatstuff.com/fresnel-lenses.html

scenes.say: Old lighthouses wasted half their light.

image.subject: a tall stone lighthouse on a rocky coast at night in a storm, a small sailing ship far out on dark waves
image.show: the lamp at the top gives only a weak yellow glow that spreads in every direction and fades into the rain, the ship barely sees it, dark teal sea, the illustration fills the whole frame from top edge to bottom edge, no empty border

scenes.motion: rain sweeps across, waves roll and break on the rocks, the weak glow flickers; the distant ship rocks on the swell

scenes.say: A flame shines everywhere: into the sky, onto the rocks. Far out at sea, a faint glow.

image.subject: inside the lantern room at the top of an old lighthouse, an oil lamp with a curved metal reflector behind it
image.show: rays of amber light leaving the flame in every direction, most going up to the ceiling and down to the floor, only a few rays heading out through the window to the sea, a red highlight on the wasted rays, one single picture, the illustration fills the whole frame from top edge to bottom edge

scenes.motion: the flame flickers and the amber rays spread out in all directions; the rays going up and down glow red and fade; only a few thin rays reach the window

scenes.say: A giant glass lens could focus it. But it would be huge, heavy, and thick enough to swallow the light.

image.subject: a huge solid round glass lens, as thick as a millstone, standing in front of a lighthouse lamp
image.show: two lighthouse workers straining to lift it with ropes, the glass so thick that the light behind it looks dim and green, a heavy wooden frame creaking, the illustration fills the whole frame from top edge to bottom edge, no empty border

scenes.motion: the workers pull on the ropes and the heavy lens barely lifts, then sinks back; the dim light behind the glass wavers

scenes.say: So how do you throw a flame twenty miles?

image.subject: close view from behind of an 1820s lighthouse keeper in a dark wool coat standing on the iron railing gallery at the very top of a lighthouse at dusk, looking out over a wide dark sea
image.show: only the top railing and lantern glass are visible, the keeper fills the lower third, a weak oil lamp glow beside him, the far horizon, first stars, exterior view only, early 19th century, no aircraft, the illustration fills the whole frame from top edge to bottom edge, no empty border

scenes.motion: wind tugs at the keeper's coat, the sea glitters below, clouds drift across the dusk sky

scenes.say: A French engineer, Augustin Fresnel, saw that only a lens's curved surface bends the light.

image.subject: a cross-section diagram of a thick convex glass lens, seen from the side
image.show: amber light rays bending only where they cross the curved outer surfaces, the thick glass middle shaded grey as unnecessary, a red highlight on the curved surfaces, plain cream background, the illustration fills the whole frame from top edge to bottom edge

scenes.motion: the amber rays travel into the lens and bend at the curved surfaces; the grey middle slowly fades out

scenes.say: He cut away the thick middle, kept the curves as rings of glass prisms around the flame.

image.subject: a tall beehive-shaped Fresnel lighthouse lens made of many concentric rings of glass prisms in a brass frame, a lamp glowing inside
image.show: the rings catching the flame's light and turning it into one straight bright beam pointing out to the right, brass and glass gleaming, the illustration fills the whole frame from top edge to bottom edge, no empty border

scenes.motion: the lamp glows brighter, light runs through the glass rings and gathers into one straight beam; the lens turns slowly

scenes.say: In 1823 the first one was lit at Cordouan, in France. Its beam reached the horizon, over twenty miles out.

image.subject: an elegant tall stone lighthouse standing on a rock island in an estuary at night
image.show: one strong straight warm white-gold beam of light shining horizontally far across calm dark water to a small sailing ship on the horizon, stars above, early 19th century, no people, no aircraft, the beam is warm gold not red, the illustration fills the whole frame from top edge to bottom edge, no empty border

scenes.motion: the beam sweeps slowly across the water and passes over the far ship; small waves glitter under it

scenes.say: Those stepped rings never left. Look closely at a car's tail light: Fresnel's rings, in plastic.

image.subject: a close-up of a modern car's red tail light at night on a wet street
image.show: the red plastic cover showing fine stepped ridges and rings, glowing, reflections on wet asphalt, the illustration fills the whole frame from top edge to bottom edge, no empty border

scenes.motion: the tail light brightens as if the brakes are pressed, the rings glow; raindrops run down the plastic; street reflections ripple

scenes.say: Nothing is ordinary once you see how it works.
scenes.motion: the beam sweeps slowly across the water; the lighthouse stands steady under the stars

people_rule: People are anonymous lighthouse workers and keepers. Augustin Fresnel is named but not shown. Never invented dialogue.
